{"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"Skill use is triggered by the situation, not remembered — the rungs cover loop debt, and skills fire on things the graph cannot see","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"An agent's use of reflow2's SKILLS must not decay over a session while its use of the TOOLS holds. Measured on reflow2's own repo, 2026-07-31, in a long session: `loop_status` was called unprompted throughout and every write went through `record_change`, two-sided checksum accepts and one-export-per-commit — but exactly two skills were loaded all session, and both only because the user typed a slash command. `impact-check`, `link-artifacts`, `capture-intent`, `revise-design`, `check-health` and `report-friction` were never loaded. THE THREE BL-74 RUNGS ARE ALL `verified` AND THIS STILL HAPPENED, which is the finding: they are working as designed and do not reach this.

THE STRUCTURAL REASON. The rungs compute LOOP DEBT — a property of graph state, which is what `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` correctly insists on. Skills fire on SITUATIONS: about to change code, just wrote a file, the user just shared an idea. The graph cannot see any of those, so the trigger mechanism covers one half of the problem and structurally cannot reach the other. That is why `impact-check` was dropped hardest — nothing in the system knows an edit is coming, and by the time the graph could tell, the edit has happened and the blast radius is a post-mortem rather than a check.

WHAT COST SOMETHING, honestly: `impact-check` was never run before changing `snapshot_node`, `delete_edge` and `delete_node`; the blast radius was reasoned about by hand instead of computed. `link-artifacts` was never loaded and a stale `art:nodes` checksum was nearly shipped — caught only by grepping after the export, which then required restoring the export and redoing it. `check-health` cost nothing, because `detect_defects` was run bare and did catch the island.

CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, in the order the evidence supports, NOT a decided design. (1) Extend the PostToolUse hook from COUNTING writes to matching SHAPES — a file edit with no ChangeEvent in the window means impact-check, an artifact checksum drift means link-artifacts. `req:nudge-covers-bypass` already arms the nudge on file-edit events and already names impact-check and link-artifacts, and is `verified`; what is missing is the shape-matching, not the trigger. (2) A refusal, where refusing is honest — reflow2's strongest mechanism, proven three times in this session alone — but only where skipping is genuinely wrong, because a guard that punishes correct work is the failure this project keeps naming.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS SESSION: BL-74 called this adoption-critical and found it in the author's own fleet, self-reported by the driving agent. This is the same failure observed from inside, on a session with MORE context about reflow2 than a consumer's agent will have — so it is likely a best case rather than a typical one.","status":"accepted"}
